body:
@annevk, I put together the changes based on the outline here:
- Call flow: https://github.com/w3c/ServiceWorker/issues/870#issuecomment-241341776
- Expected behavior: https://github.com/w3c/ServiceWorker/issues/870#issuecomment-245559217

I'd appreciate your review.

/cc @domenic @jakearchibald
Note for others interested in this PR, we're discussing the general design in https://github.com/whatwg/fetch/pull/383.

@annevk, I basically regarded the environment concept and the environment settings object concept are covariant. So, I defined it as "an environment settings object is an environment." and later in the service worker, I'll use the environment to enumerate all the clients there. Please take a look.
Self-note: ~~destroy the environment object after when its values are set up to the resulting environment settings object. (missed it.)~~

> I'm also a little unsure about naming. We have "environment settings object" which effectively means global object. This adds "environment" which means something like "future/reserved global object".

Open to renaming it. I absolutely want a better name for it if we can get one.

> It's also a little weird still that we grab some state from request to create something new and then grab something from the newly created thing and tack it on request. That just doesn't seem quite right.

I don't think I can help here. The only state I copy from request to environment is the request's url which the newly created environment has to have. (Note that I tried to factor the creation URL out to environment as both environment and environment settings object need this info.) And the only state I copy from the created environment to request is its id, which is the whole idea this patch suggests. I think it makes sense as a navigation works in this way.
Are you saying that this is also how Chrome/Samsung Internet would engineer this setup? @wanderview would we use this setup in Firefox?

I'll dig into it again, but this is what I found sometime ago: https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/322#issuecomment-200229641

Basically, Chromium will have to implement something similar to the reserved id, store it somewhere like in the service worker provider and later relate the id to the actual frame id when the frame and the document are created. So, I think, in order to expose the `FetchEvent.reservedClientId` and `FetchEvent.targetClientId`, we'll have to implement the similar logic. It'll be great if @wanderview and @mattto cross-checks if this setup is good to implement. Please check out this simplified flow to help your understanding: https://github.com/w3c/ServiceWorker/issues/870#issuecomment-241341776

Also, I'd appreciate your comments on calling the match service worker registration algorithm twice: once for main resource fetch and the other for attaching a controller after the global is created. This is due to the fact that it's not easy to pass the captured state around between navigate/fetch/SW.

Having thought a bit more on this, matching the registration twice is awkward. I think we can do better as we now have the environment concept where we can store the matched registration. For this, we'd have to pass this environment along with the request as @annevk asked above.

So, the idea is:
- Match a service worker registration with request's url
- Create an environment and set all their internal slots properly including the service worker registration internal slot to the matched registration
- Check (in Handle Fetch) if the reserved client's service worker registration is not null and its active worker is not null to dispatch fetch event. (For subresource fetch, client's registration should be used instead of the reserved client's registration.)

(With this change, we don't need to store the active worker on the global objects. Also, by passing the environment along with a request, we can remove request's target browsing context internal slot. We can use reserved client's target browsing context instead.)

For worker clients, we can basically do the same and will pass the entire environment settings object (instead of an environment) that is set with the matched registration to fetch. This means the type of "reserved client" internal slot to request should be "null or an environment or an environment settings object".

I think this matches the implementations more precisely, at least Chromium. @wanderview, would it make sense for Gecko? (Note that this doesn't change the originally proposed behavior in this PR. Both matching the registration twice and matching it once / storing in an environment will use the latest active worker always.)
@mattto, @kinu I'd appreciate your comments on this.

Having reviewed Chromium's navigation part of the code again, I believe the structure I'm trying to spec in this PR would be implementable.

The current implementation is explained in https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/322#issuecomment-200229641 The gist is when it initializes the request handler for a navigation request (`ServiceWorkerRequestHandler::InitializeForNavigation` - largely corresponding to initializing a request to pass to Handle Fetch) it already sets up the |provider_host|'s client (request's client in the spec) to the new reserved client - which the spec will do with the change. The current implementation just ignores this value by setting the `FetchEvent's clientId` to null if it's a navigation request.

So for navigation requests, Chromium will need to change to set the request handler's provider_host to the source client instead of the reserved client. And add a reserved_provider_host or similar state to grab the pre-created (i.e. reserved) client and the target_provider_host's client_id.

Still would like to check what Gecko does and whether the proposed structure is implementable there.
Thanks @domenic. I'll address your comments and this change (https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/1776#issuecomment-250465276) after checking with @wanderview if Gecko has any concerns.

@wanderview, I'd like to check with you this spec change is feasible with Gecko. I'd appreciate your comments on the below questions.

Gecko's using a document id to identify a client. It generates a new document id in `nsDocShell::ChannelIntercepted` and passes it to the fetch event dispatch procedure where it seems to be planing to use this document id to set `FetcheEvent.reservedClientId` according to the comments in the code. I'd like to ask and discuss around the possibilities below:
- It seems the current client getter methods (e.g. `clients.get(id)`) are not able to grab a reserved client in fetch event's handlers as only the already-being-created documents (i.e. those set with `AddObserver(.."service-worker-get-client"..)` ) are observable in the client list. So, this needs changes I guess.
- Can Gecko define and use a new object that has the id, creation URL, reference to target browsing context and matched service worker registration instead of using a document id?
  (As an aside, I think this environment concept associated with a global is a better fit to represent what's controlled than a document as we have both window client and worker client concepts.)
- Can we do the registration matching at the beginning of a navigation (before calling fetch) as proposed in https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/1776#issuecomment-250465276?
- Gecko will need to capture the target DocShell's associated Window's client id during a navigation. (Chromium will need to add this as well.)

Had a chat with @wanderview. We agreed to proceed with this PR. I'll address the comments given so far and the changes outlined in https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/1776#issuecomment-250465276, and ask review.

@annevk @domenic, I uploaded new snapshots having addressed the comments and the additional changes discussed. I believe this outlined flow will help your understanding: https://github.com/w3c/ServiceWorker/issues/870#issuecomment-241341776 Please take a look.
- Summary
  - An environment has |id|, |creation URL|, |target browsing context|, |service worker|.
  - An environment is created during a navigation to represent a reserved client to SW.
  - Later in the navigation step when the environment settings object is created, the reserved environment's states are copied to the environment settings object. (that environment is destroyed here.)
  - For other occasions where an environment settings object is created (e.g. initial browsing context creation, etc.), the environment part of the states are set to initial values. (|id| is set to a new opaque string.)
  - Worker creation is similar, but in this case, an environment settings object is created before invoking fetch, so no separate environment is created.
  - Service worker registration matching is executed in SW's Handle Fetch algorithm (WIP).
  - Once a active service worker is set to the reserved client(environment), that service worker's registration's waiting worker won't promote until all the client including this client will be unloaded; this resolves my previous concern about having different service worker versions for the main resource request and its subresource requests.
  - SW will expose the reserved client's id, target client's id as well as the (source) client's id to fetch event handlers (WIP).
  - SW's clients-getter-methods will enumerate service worker clients including environments and environment settings objects depending on the given options to the methods (WIP).

I should have time to review this tomorrow, but if you have a chance to remove the re-wrapping and blank-line-removing, that would make things easier to review. It's much better now than it was though :)
Sounds great. I updated the snapshot having removed the re-wrapping and blank-line-removing. Please take a look.
@domenic, I updated the snapshot having addressed your comments. Please take a look.
Thanks for the comments, @domenic. I uploaded a new snapshot having addressed them. /cc @annevk
LGTM with those last few nits fixed. I assume we don't have a testing plan here because this is is about new stuff? That's probably okay.
